d: In-game UI containers hold SurfaceGuis, BillboardGuis, and GuiObjects that you want to display in the 3D space.
h:
In-game UI containers hold GuiObjects that you want to display within your game's 3D world.

  • A SurfaceGui allows for the rendering of UI objects onto a part's surface in the 3D world while also allowing for basic user interaction to occur.
  • A BillboardGui is a container for UI objects to appear in the 3D space but always face the camera.

Surface UI

Similar to Decals and Textures, UI objects such as TextLabels and ImageLabels parented to a SurfaceGui face the same direction as the surface they're on, editable through the SurfaceGui.Face property.

To apply a SurfaceGui to an in-game BasePart, simply parent it to that part and set the SurfaceGui.Face property. Child UI objects then appear on that face of the parent part.

<div class="gcell" markdown="1">
    <img src="../assets/studio/explorer/Part-SurfaceGui-ImageLabel.png" width="320" />

<div class="gcell" markdown="1">
    <img src="../assets/studio/properties/SurfaceGui-Face-Top.png" width="320" />
</div>

Alternatively, you can place the SurfaceGui inside a container like StarterGui and then set its Adornee property to any BasePart, as well as the target Face. Setting Adornee overrides direct parent association, allowing for more flexibility in placement since it can be set from a script during runtime.

<div class="gcell" markdown="1">
    <img src="../assets/studio/explorer/StarterGui-SurfaceGui.png" width="320" />

<div class="gcell" markdown="1">
    <img src="../assets/studio/properties/SurfaceGui-Adornee-Face.png" width="320" />
</div>

Interactive UI elements like ImageButtons and TextButtons inside a SurfaceGui will only receive user input if they are parented to the player's PlayerGui, typically via placing the SurfaceGui inside StarterGui as noted above. Additionally, the part's CanQuery property must be true for the interactive UI element to receive input.

To assist in choosing the correct face for a SurfaceGui, right-click the target part and select Show Orientation Indicator. This displays a blue circle with an F and a line attached to the object's Front face, and a green arrow that points in the direction of the object's Top face.

Size and position

The "canvas" of a SurfaceGui occupies the entire Face of the parent or Adornee part. As a best practice, it's recommended that you use scale values for the size and position of child UI objects like ImageLabels. You can also apply a UIAspectRatioConstraint to children of the SurfaceGui to maintain their desired aspect ratio regardless of the face's size.

Occlusion mode

The AlwaysOnTop property determines whether the SurfaceGui will render over top of 3D content or be occluded by it. When set to false (default), the SurfaceGui renders like other 3D content and is occluded by other 3D objects. When set to true, it always renders over top of 3D content and it is not influenced by brightness/light in the 3D environment.

Brightness and light influence

Brightness and LightInfluence work in conjunction to determine how environmental light affects the UI content of the SurfaceGui.

Brightness determines the factor by which emitted light is scaled in a range of 0 to 1000, letting you match the SurfaceGui to its environment. For instance, a video billboard can be brightened inside a dark room by increasing Brightness to 10.

LightInfluence controls how much the SurfaceGui is influenced by lighting in the place, in a range from 0 to 1. Setting this to 1 means that surrounding lighting has complete control over the appearance, while setting it to 0 means that the lighting has no effect.

Note that Brightness is inaccessible in Studio and has no effect when either LightInfluence is 1 or AlwaysOnTop is true.

Distance visibility

MaxDistance controls how far from the camera the SurfaceGui will be displayed before it stops rendering. A value of 0 means there is no limit and it will render infinitely far away. The default value of 1000 works fine for most cases.

For SurfaceGuis that appear outdoors, it's recommended that MaxDistance is high enough to ensure that the container's UI is sufficiently small on the screen when it appears or disappears, minimizing the sudden pop‑in/out effect.

Display order

If multiple SurfaceGui containers exist on the same face, you can layer them by Z‑index through their ZOffset property (changing this does not visually "lift" or "sink" the container from the surface).

Billboard UI

The BillboardGui container displays UI objects in the 3D space but, unlike SurfaceGui, children of a BillboardGui always face the camera. This container is useful for displaying front‑facing info above in-game objects such as health meters or names above player characters, markers to guide players to an object in the 3D world, and more.

To link a BillboardGui to an in-game BasePart or Attachment, simply parent it to that part or attachment and, if desired, adjust its size/position.

<div class="gcell" markdown="1">
    <img src="../assets/studio/explorer/Part-BillboardGui-ImageLabel.png" width="320" />

<div class="gcell" markdown="1">
    <img src="../assets/studio/explorer/Part-Attachment-BillboardGui-ImageLabel.png" width="320" />
</div>

Alternatively, you can place the BillboardGui inside a container like StarterGui and then set its Adornee property to any BasePart or Attachment. This method offers more flexibility in placement since Adornee can be set from a script during runtime, for example to place a BillboardGui over the head of player characters during runtime.

Interactive UI elements like ImageButtons and TextButtons inside a BillboardGui will only receive user input if they are parented to the player's PlayerGui, typically via placing the BillboardGui inside StarterGui as noted above.

Size and position

For billboard sizing, the scale components of the Size property set the billboard's stud size in 3D space. For example, a setting of {10, 0},{2, 0} (UDim2.fromScale(10, 2)) forms a billboard with a 10:2 aspect ratio that scales larger or smaller depending on its distance from the camera.

For positioning, the StudsOffset property shifts the billboard canvas on the X axis (left/right), Y axis (up/down), and Z axis (forward/back) relative to the camera.

When creating a size-scaled BillboardGui that contains a TextLabel, it's useful to enable the label's TextScaled property so that its text scales along with the billboard canvas as the camera distance changes.

Occlusion mode

The AlwaysOnTop property determines whether the BillboardGui will render over top of 3D content or be occluded by it. When set to false (default), the BillboardGui renders like other 3D content and is occluded by other 3D objects. When set to true, it always renders over top of 3D content and it is not influenced by brightness/light in the 3D environment.

Brightness and light influence

Brightness and LightInfluence work in conjunction to determine how environmental light affects the UI content of the BillboardGui.

Brightness determines the factor by which emitted light is scaled in a range of 0 to 1000, letting you match the BillboardGui to its environment. For instance, a video billboard can be brightened inside a dark room by increasing Brightness to 10.

LightInfluence controls how much the BillboardGui is influenced by lighting in the place, in a range from 0 to 1. Setting this to 1 means that surrounding lighting has complete control over the appearance, while setting it to 0 means that the lighting has no effect.

Note that Brightness is inaccessible in Studio and has no effect when either LightInfluence is 1 or AlwaysOnTop is true.

Distance visibility

MaxDistance controls how far from the camera the BillboardGui will be displayed before it stops rendering. A value of 0 or inf (default) means there is no limit and it will render infinitely far away.

kid.simple: Sometimes you want UI inside the 3D world instead of flat on the screen, like a scoreboard on a wall or a name floating over someone's head. A `SurfaceGui` sticks UI onto one face of a part, like a poster. A `BillboardGui` floats in the world and always turns to face the camera. This page shows how to attach them, size them, light them, and decide how far away they can be seen.
kid.analogy: A `SurfaceGui` is like a poster glued to a wall: walk around and you see it from the side. A `BillboardGui` is like a balloon with a smiley face that always turns to look at you.
keyPoints: Parent a `SurfaceGui` to a part and set its `Face` (like Front or Top) to choose which side shows the UI.
Or keep the `SurfaceGui` in `StarterGui` and set its `Adornee` to the part; this is needed for buttons on it to be clickable.
For clickable `SurfaceGui` buttons, the part's `CanQuery` must also be true.
Use scale values for the size and position of UI inside a `SurfaceGui` so it fits any face size.
`AlwaysOnTop` makes the UI draw over 3D objects instead of being hidden behind them.
`Brightness` and `LightInfluence` control how the world's lighting affects the UI; `LightInfluence` 0 means lighting has no effect.
`MaxDistance` sets how far away the UI stops drawing; 0 means no limit.
For a `BillboardGui`, scale values in `Size` are measured in studs, and `StudsOffset` shifts it, for example up above a head.

terms.SurfaceGui: A container that shows UI flat on one side of a part.
terms.BillboardGui: A container that shows UI floating in the world, always turned toward the camera.
terms.Face: Which side of the part the `SurfaceGui` uses: Front, Back, Top, Bottom, Left, or Right.
terms.Adornee: The part (or attachment) the UI should appear on, even if the UI is stored somewhere else like `StarterGui`.
terms.occluded: Hidden behind something. A sign behind a wall is occluded unless `AlwaysOnTop` is on.
terms.LightInfluence: From 0 to 1. At 1 the UI gets darker at night like the rest of the world; at 0 it stays the same.
terms.Brightness: How strongly the UI glows, from 0 to 1000. It only matters when `LightInfluence` is below 1 and `AlwaysOnTop` is off.
terms.StudsOffset: Moves a billboard a set number of studs from its part. `Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)` lifts it 3 studs up.
terms.scale vs. offset: Scale is a fraction of the space (0.5 = half). Offset is an exact number of pixels.
terms.ZOffset: Decides which `SurfaceGui` draws on top when two are on the same face. It does not physically move it.
terms.aspect ratio: Width compared to height. A size of 10 by 2 studs is a 10:2 (or 5:1) ratio.

example.title: Float a name tag over a part
example.place: Script in ServerScriptService (with a part named Sign in Workspace)
example.code:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local part = Workspace:WaitForChild("Sign")

local billboard = Instance.new("BillboardGui")
billboard.Size = UDim2.fromScale(6, 2) -- 6 studs wide, 2 studs tall
billboard.StudsOffset = Vector3.new(0, 3, 0) -- 3 studs above the part
billboard.MaxDistance = 100 -- hide when farther than 100 studs
billboard.Parent = part

local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
label.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1) -- fill the whole billboard
label.BackgroundTransparency = 1 -- no background box
label.Text = "Welcome!"
label.TextScaled = true -- text grows and shrinks with the billboard
label.Parent = billboard
explain: We find the part called Sign.
We make a `BillboardGui` 6 by 2 studs and lift it 3 studs above the part with `StudsOffset`.
We stop drawing it beyond 100 studs to keep things tidy.
We add a `TextLabel` that fills the billboard and turn on `TextScaled` so the words fit as you move closer or farther.

watchOut: Buttons on a `SurfaceGui` or `BillboardGui` that sits inside a part will not respond to clicks. Put the GUI in `StarterGui` and set `Adornee` instead.
Wrong side? Right-click the part and choose Show Orientation Indicator to see which way is Front.
Using offset (pixels) on a `SurfaceGui` can make UI too big or too small on different parts. Use scale.
If your sign is too dark at night, lower `LightInfluence` or turn on `AlwaysOnTop`.
